name: Adrenyx
description: Adrenyx is a precision-engineered synthetic catecholamine cascade delivered via autoinjector, flooding the bloodstream with a calibrated blend of epinephrine analogues and cortisol suppressants. It produces a controlled adrenal surge without the cortisol spike that causes post-combat cognitive fog. Standard issue for Lazarus-contracted corporate security.
effects: Dramatically elevated heart rate and cardiac output
Peripheral vasoconstriction redirecting blood to major muscle groups
Increased grip strength and explosive movement speed
Heightened sensory acuity for approximately 4 minutes post-injection
Suppression of fatigue signals for duration
side_effects: Severe tachycardia if stacked with other stimulants
Hypertensive crash causing dizziness and nausea
Risk of cardiac arrhythmia with repeated same-day dosing
Dependency develops within 6-8 weeks of regular use
cultural_context: Adrenyx is what corporate security teams pop before breaching a hostile floor. It's considered a 'clean' combat drug — respectable enough that Tier 3 middle managers who run weekend militia cosplay also acquire it. On the Gray Zone, stolen Adrenyx autoinjectors are currency, traded for food or weapons. Street users often mistime dosing because they lack the training to read the onset window.
story_hooks: A runner finds a crate of Adrenyx autoinjectors with Lazarus lot numbers that don't exist in any public database — suggesting a black-budget formulation more potent than the commercial version.
A corporate security captain is burning through her Adrenyx prescription at three times normal rate, and her supervisor needs to know if she's compromised or just scared.
the Gray Zone version of Adrenyx has been cut with a dopaminergic compound that creates euphoria alongside the surge — someone is deliberately engineering addiction into the street supply.
